samples.summary: The new post-await `disposed` guard is bypassed by `EditorAPI.paste()`, a third async write that can outlive the editor
samples.evidence: The diff adds `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;` after the await in `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` (text-editor.ts:4254) and rewrites the `disposed` docstring to claim there are exactly "two writes that can outlive the editor" (text-editor.ts:361-366). There is a third: `EditorAPI.paste()` in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3905-3937 awaits `navigator.clipboard.read()` / `readText()` and then calls `textEditor.pasteContent({html, text})` at editor.ts:3928 and :3936. `pasteContent` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1659-1668) checks `readOnly` and `pasting` but NOT `disposed`, and `editor.ts`'s `dispose()` (editor.ts:4364) sets no flag that neuters the `api` object — the read-only neutering at editor.ts:4430-4452 is the only place `api.paste` is replaced. So a context-menu paste whose clipboard permission prompt resolves after the host unmounts writes through a disposed editor into a document nothing renders — precisely the harm the new guard was added for. Fix belongs on `pasteContent` (or on `EditorAPI.paste` after its awaits), not on the new code.

samples.summary: Wiring `requestLayoutRefresh = recomputeLayout` consumes `dirtyBlockIds`, so the deferred paint's own `recomputeLayout` runs cache-disabled — a full-document re-measure per edit
samples.evidence: `recomputeLayout` clears the incremental-layout dirty set at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1534 (`dirtyBlockIds = undefined;`) after passing it to `computeLayout` (:1526). `computeLayout` only reuses the cache when the dirty set is non-null: `const canUseCache = cache != null && dirtyBlockIds != null && ...` (packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:456-459). With the new wiring (editor.ts:2531), an interior `requestRender()` inside an undo unit now runs `recomputeLayout()` — consuming and clearing the dirty set — and the replayed paint afterwards goes through `renderWithScroll` → `render()` → `recomputeLayout()` again (editor.ts:2208-2211, 2434-2438) with `dirtyBlockIds === undefined`, i.e. cache bypassed and every block re-measured. Since `handleInput` is now always inside a unit, that means at least one full-document layout pass per keystroke (two or more when `deleteSelectionImpl`'s several interior `requestRender()` calls fire, text-editor.ts:3937/3971/4022/4058/4087) on documents of exactly the size issue #1045 is about. Nothing in the diff re-arms the dirty set for the deferred paint.

samples.summary: Three sibling Yorkie stores still use the depth-based undo floor this change replaced, and their comments still point at it as the pattern to mirror
samples.evidence: The diff replaces `undoFloor` (a depth) with `undoFloorMark` (entry identity) in `YorkieDocStore` because Yorkie shifts the oldest entry off a full 50-entry stack. The same length-vs-depth comparison remains in packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:353 (`this.doc.getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor`), packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:654, and packages/frontend/src/app/board/yorkie-board-store.ts:514 — all three of which document themselves as copies ("Mirrors `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor`", yorkie-note-store.ts:125, yorkie-slides-store.ts:345). Those comments and docs/design/notes/notes.md:399 now describe a contract that no longer exists in the referenced store, and the eviction bug survives in three packages. Pre-existing there, but the change is what makes the mirror stale.

samples.summary: Every keystroke on a MemDocStore host now enters `batch()`, adding a document clone plus up to three full `JSON.stringify` passes per character
samples.evidence: `handleInput` and `deleteSelection` now always call `doc.batch(...)` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1020, :3863), so on the MemDocStore hosts — slides text boxes (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:446 → packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:668), the docs demo and the visual harness — each keystroke now runs `cloneDocument(this.doc)` + `JSON.stringify(beforeClone)` + `JSON.stringify(top)` at memory.ts:256-259 and another `JSON.stringify(cloneDocument(this.doc))` at :289, on top of the clone `snapshot()` already takes. Previously typing touched none of this. Correctness is unaffected; the cost is O(document) per character on any MemDocStore host holding a large document.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The diff's new post-await re-validation `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;` exists at text-editor.ts:4254, and the `disposed` field doc at text-editor.ts:363-369 asserts there are exactly two writes that can outlive the editor (grep confirms `disposed` is read only at 1609 and 4254). A third such write exists and bypasses it: `EditorAPI.paste` at editor.ts:3905-3938 awaits `navigator.clipboard.read()` (3910), `blob.text()` (3917/3923) and `readText()` (3935), then calls `textEditor.pasteContent(...)` at 3928/3936. `pasteContent` (text-editor.ts:1659-1668) checks only `readOnly` and `pasting`, never `disposed`, and for payloads under the large-paste threshold `runPaste` (1588-1601) runs `job()` synchronously at 1596, so `deferPaste`'s `if (!this.disposed)` guard at 1609 is never reached — `applyPastePlan` (1544) writes to `this.doc`. Nothing neuters the closure: `editor.ts:4364-4395` calls `textEditor?.dispose()` (4374) but never clears the captured `textEditor`, and the only replacement of `api.paste` is the read-only allowlist at editor.ts:4430-4452, which does not apply outside view-only mode. The path is reachable from the frontend context menu at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-context-menu.tsx:272 (`void editor!.paste()`), i.e. a permission prompt resolving after unmount. This is squarely in the blast-radius lane (a new guard with another entry point reaching the same mutation) and blocking at major.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the repo. `recomputeLayout` passes `dirtyBlockIds` to `computeLayout` and then clears it (editor.ts:1526,1534), and `computeLayout` only reuses cached block lines when `dirtyBlockIds != null` (layout.ts:456-459, gate used at layout.ts:535). The new wiring assigns that same closure as the measure-without-paint seam (editor.ts:2531), and `TextEditor.requestRender` calls it whenever `undoUnitDepth > 0` instead of painting (text-editor.ts:734-743). On unit exit, `withUndoUnit` replays `this.requestRender()` (text-editor.ts:3846-3849), which now reaches `hostRequestRender` = `renderWithScroll` (editor.ts:2473) -> `render()` (editor.ts:2434-2436) -> `recomputeLayout()` (editor.ts:2208-2210) with `dirtyBlockIds === undefined`, so `canUseCache` is false and every block is re-measured via `layoutBlock` (layout.ts:538). This is reachable on the plain typing path: `handleInput` wraps its write in `withUndoUnit`, calls `markDirty` at text-editor.ts:1035 and then an interior `requestRender()` at text-editor.ts:1047 which consumes the freshly armed set; that path does not call `invalidateLayout`, so the cache exists but is bypassed. The only other writers of the set are `markDirty` (editor.ts:1582-1587) and `invalidateLayout` (editor.ts:1673-1676, which also clears it) — nothing re-arms it before the deferred paint, and the change's own lessons note (docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-lessons.md:37-45) does not address it. No guard makes it unreachable, and it is in this lens's lane (an invariant the layout-cache consumer relies on, violated at a site outside the diff), so no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Cmd+Shift+V's post-await write has no `disposed` guard, unlike every other deferred paste write. This delta's new test pins this async path as a supported one-undo-unit action, so the missing guard is now load-bearing.
finding.evidence: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4242-4256) awaits `navigator.clipboard.readText()` and then, with no re-validation, calls `this.saveSnapshot()` and opens a `withUndoUnit` batch that deletes the selection and inserts text. The only other write that resumes after a yield does re-validate: `deferPaste` at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1606-1608 — `if (!this.disposed) job();` with the comment "The host can unmount during the frame this waited for; writing through a disposed editor would mutate a document nothing renders." A user pressing Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+V and immediately navigating away (docs-view unmount → `dispose()`) resolves the clipboard promise after teardown and writes a full select-all replacement into the store through a torn-down editor. The fix belongs on the new code path in text-editor.ts (add the `disposed` check, mirroring line 1608).

verdict.reason: The finding is an absence claim — that the Cmd+Shift+V post-await write has no `disposed` guard — and the guard exists. In the working tree, `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4243-4265) awaits `navigator.clipboard.readText()` at line 4245 and then, before any mutation, re-validates at line 4254 with `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;`. Only after that does it call `this.saveSnapshot()` (4255) and open the `withUndoUnit` batch that deletes the selection and inserts text (4256-4261). The in-code comment at 4247-4253 states the intent directly: 'This is the second write that resumes after a yield, so it needs the same two re-validations `deferPaste` does.' The guard is in fact stricter than the `deferPaste` comparison site the finding cites (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1609, `if (!this.disposed) job();`), since it also short-circuits on `pasting`. `disposed` is the same field `deferPaste` relies on: declared at line 369 and set true in `dispose()` at line 6062, so the exact scenario described (Cmd+Shift+V then navigate away → dispose() → clipboard promise resolves post-teardown) returns at 4254 and never reaches `saveSnapshot()`. The finding's prescribed fix ('add the disposed check, mirroring line 1608') is already implemented. The reviewer's cited range (4242-4256) is off by one from the current function body and their reported empty grep for `this.disposed` in this file contradicts a plain grep, indicating they read a stale revision.

finding.summary: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` writes after its await without checking `this.pasting`, so it can land inside a large paste's yield gap that every other write path is guarded against.
finding.evidence: The `pasting` flag is honoured by handleCompositionStart (text-editor.ts:893), handleInput (967), handleKeyDown (1056), pasteContent (1664/1676) and mousedown (1843) — all with the comment "A large paste is mid-yield; its write owns the caret." `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` (4242) neither sets nor checks it: Cmd+Shift+V → await clipboard read → user starts a large Cmd+V paste (runPaste sets `pasting = true` at 1598 and yields) → the plain-text promise resolves and writes deleteSelection + insertPlainText against a caret/selection the in-flight paste owns, inside its own batch. The new test in this delta (packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts:432) treats this async path as a first-class composite action, which is what makes the unguarded gap worth closing. Fix belongs in text-editor.ts's plain-paste path.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` writes after its await without checking `this.pasting`. It does check. At packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4254, immediately after `await navigator.clipboard.readText()` (4245) and before `saveSnapshot()`/`withUndoUnit(deleteSelection + insertPlainText)` (4255-4261), the method executes `if (this.disposed || this.pasting) return;`. The comment at 4247-4253 spells out the same reasoning the finding demands ("writing while `pasting` would land inside a large paste's yield gap, against a caret that paste's pending write owns"), and it also re-validates `disposed`. The described interleaving (Cmd+Shift+V awaits clipboard, concurrent large Cmd+V sets `pasting = true` at 1599 and yields, plain-text promise resolves) therefore returns early instead of writing. The guard is present at exactly the location the finding says the fix belongs.
